statement.text: Let $H(n)$ be the smallest integer $l$ such that there exist $k<l$ with $(k^n-1,l^n-1)=1$. Is it true that $H(n)=3$ infinitely often? (That is, $(2^n-1,3^n-1)=1$ infinitely often?) Estimate $H(n)$. Is it true that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that, for all $\epsilon>0$, $ H(n) > \exp(n^{(c-\epsilon)/\log\log n}) $ for infinitely many $n$ and $ H(n) < \exp(n^{(c+\epsilon)/\log\log n}) $ for all large enough $n$? Does a similar upper bound hold for the smallest $k$ such that $(k^n-1,2^n-1)=1$?
